I was excited for this game after I saw a Quick Look video for it on
. This game looked, to me, like
, but in space!
And it is. Sort of. When you're in combat, anyway, and most of the time you will be. Your starships exchange fire with enemies while darting in-between asteroids and moons, effectively using them as directional "cover". Space, it seems, is simply
with asteroids (which I will admit is a little unrealistic), but nevertheless these debris-strewn starfields provide you with dynamic (and occasionally, changing) battlefields to fight upon.
Aside from that, combat mechanics themselves are quite simple. Mostly you will be attacking enemy vessels, and there are four ways to do it: With lasers (long range), plasma cannons (short range), torpedoes (area-of-effect), and fighter jets. For defense and utility, you have cloaking devices and sensor sweeps. That's it! These six mechanics provide the primary functions of your ships. While this may be too simplistic for some, they nevertheless provide enough complexity to allow for emergent tactics.
The only other way to change how your ships work is to build "wonders" for your civilization, and each one will grant your fleet additional powers. Usually this is fun, as the powers are interesting and vary widely, but unfortunately, it is entirely random as to which planets can build each type, and if a civilization gets lucky and acquires the best wonders early on, you will find that they have a distinct advantage over everyone else.
I was a little disappointed that there weren't any customization options for the starships. Your ships
change shape when you add new modules to them, but there are no purely cosmetic options whatsoever (like paint jobs, etc). While that
be a minor gripe, it can actually become problematic when you are fighting against enemies that have ships that look almost identical to yours, and this happens a lot because there are only three types of ship construction, and a proper game has eight players.
The other main thing you do in this game, aside from fighting battles and building your ships, is manage your colonies. This part of the game is reasonably fun, but it mostly just boils down to looking at menus and spending your accumulated resources. There isn't a lot of depth here, and it seems to just serve as a bookend to the combat missions.
The diplomacy system isn't all that deep, either. Aside from declaring war and making peace, there isn't much else you can do - there are no trade agreements, no cease-fires or non-aggression pacts, really no minutae to speak of. This area of the game is sorely lacking, and in some ways does not even feel finished.
Which leads me to my next point. Polish! This game sorely needs it! I found plenty of spelling errors in the text, and the clunky animations in combat (particularly when ships explode) left something to be desired. It almost feels like the game was released too early, or perhaps the project was prematurely abandoned.
There's also a marked lack of features. For instance, there is no multiplayer! Why? This game would be a lot of fun against a friend, but instead you're stuck playing against the lackluster AI.
On that note, I think I should mention that this game is REALLY, REALLY EASY. Even on "impossible" difficulty, I found the game to be ridiculously easy regardless of the chosen win condition. The enemies are simply too easy to outsmart. Occasionally they will even take stupid actions on their own, like firing a torpedo point-blank into a planet or moon, causing area-of-effect damage to themselves and their allies. The AI seriously needs work in order to feel complete.
Finally, this game is short. You're looking at only a few hours per playthrough, even with eight players and an "epic" sized galaxy. Certain win conditions can extend it, but the basic win conditions of "all" or "population" victories will end in extremely short order. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but it means that this game is a more casual experience than you may be used to, especially if you're a
fan.
I know what you're thinking. I've trashed the game quite a bit, so why am I recommending it? The answer is simple. It's
. The combat is solid and the empire-building is too, even if it's a little on the simplistic side. It's a great game to play when you've got a few hours spare and, perhaps, don't want to commit to starting a huge, long game of
or
.
I enjoyed this game, and I hope it will continue to receive support and updates so it can become the great game that it should be. For now, though, all I can say is that it's worth the money - If you get it on sale.

I remember playing the second Fancy Pants Adventure game on Kongregate back in the day, and every iteration afterwards. I'm very pleased with the evolution of this game into something even more special than it was all those years ago. Very little has changed aside from some polish, and I wouldn't have it any other way.
The controls are tight as heck, and it's ridiculously easy to build up a zen-like flow as you glide effortlessly through the levels. Not that it's easy, but it feels natural and effortless to control the Fancy Pants Man. Rarely will a death feel "wrong" or as if it wasn't your fault. The game isn't super difficult, but it's not without its moments of challenge.
The music is as upbeat as ever, very peppy and fun. It can get a little repetitive, as video game music tends to, but it's still good music regardless.
The visuals are fun, charming, and bouncy. Meant to deliberately evoke some of the fluidity that Flash offered to those willing to learn. The colors of the levels can get a little grating at time (Personally the bright orange level gave me a headache), but this could just be me.
The writing is minimal, but funny where it happens. It's witty and irreverent, but maybe not very much, largely because there's so little of it.
All in all, it's an excellent game, a fun time, and something I would absolutely recommend owning. 9/10.

A trip down memory lane for me! I always liked the Fancy Pants Adventures series ever since I found out about it on the internet, so when the time came for Brad Borne (the developer) to make World 4, he worked on a new version of the Flash SDK (Action Script 2 to Action Script 3) and released the "tech demo", World 1 Remix! After that, Brad started the 3 year long developement of World 4 (the game you are currently looking at on this page!) and I was waiting for so long that time, it felt like a Half Life 3/TF2 Pyro Update/Portal 3(?)/Super Smash Bros for the Switch sort of situation. But then one fateful day, this game's announcement date to be precise, it was revealed that World 4 would be Super Fancy Pants Adventures and it would release on Steam. That was kind of a shock to me because I never expected the Fancy Pants Adventures series to end up on Steam of all places!
Well, enough about that part. Super Fancy Pants Adventures feels like your typical Fancy Pants game, thanks to its brilliant soundtrack and excellent controls. The story is as basic as any of the other game's stories get. But overall, I really enjoyed it.
I really enjoyed every second of this game. I'd recommend it to Sonic fans (as that fact is how I got into this series in the first place), Mario fans too and anyone who's just looking for a quick game to play (yes, the game's quite short at the time of me writing this). Although I wouldn't recommend this game to people expecting multiplayer (I'm looking at you TacoGao).

I have always dreamed about becoming a proton moving at almost light speed inside a particle accelerator, and now I can re-create these dreams in this particle accelerator simulator game!
You play as a tiny white packet of protons which are stripped of all of their electrons inside a particle accelerator, or a "collider", as it is called, moving through certain obstacles, although a collider will not usually have such obstacles for the packet of protons to maneuver through, I will assume they are magnetic accelerators, as  maybe in a newer design I am not yet familiar with are already implemented in.
However, I was personally confused as to why there was only one proton shown, as normally, there would be "packets" of protons, consisting of roughly 100 billion protons per packets, with roughly 1500 packets. Although I take this as a mistake, I will not be to critical as this could of been a design choice, as having all this on your screen may be slightly distracting game-play wise.
I was also slightly dissappointed with the introduction, as I was really hoping to be able to traverse through different boosters, as this was the highlight of my particle accelerating fantasies. I was also very dissapointed with the lack of ending cutscenes, as I am still very curious as to what happens to the packet you are in control of. as there is no other protons to be able to collide with, I lost loads of fantasy filled nights thinking over the results of this specific collider. I was expecting there to be a cutscene at the end where you finally collide with another proton to cause many new particles or atoms to fling out so I could record the results. But maybe there will be a DLC, or even better, a sequel to the game which might show this.
Overall, I found this collider simulator very fun to play, although not very realistic, I had a great time achieving the fantasies I've always had.

In this sequel, we encounter some known characters, such as Amanda and Gabriel, but this isn't a social encounter, as a new problem arises, a threat bigger than ever. A gem forged in hell and passed on through greed, only to leave behind a trail of destruction and death. Hidden away through time and ages, from keeper to keeper, until the right time arrives to destroy such dangerous artifact!
New characters also await us, throughout different parts of the world, and with them, new quests arrive. In this new game, the mysterious house lets us travel through portals and visit different parts of the world, in different eras, so we can track down the powerful gem.
Once again the locations are diverse, each more beautiful than the previous ones, from Tibet to India, Madagascar to Jerusalem, the player must solve the puzzles and give the final result to the keepers of the artifacts that hold the power to destroy the gem. Each distinct location with its own story, marked by the despair caused by this evil gem.
The locations are beautiful, but generic, and that's not entirely a bad thing, as the developers did a great job portraying each specific country into 3 or 4 locations.
Visually, the sequel is slightly better from the original game, as the 3D cutscenes are improved in detail and quality, but still locked to a certain resolution. Overall visuals are very detailed and fantastic, but it's a shame this sequel suffers from the same locked resolutions as the previous title. This means
used the same engine, therefor creating the same issue with outdated resolutions. With this in mind, HoC are compromised on quality presentation, otherwise they would've been simply fantastic and mesmerizing with such beautiful scenarios available.
The gameplay works exactly as the previous title, with recurring Hidden Object scenes scattered around the chapters, and adding several objects-out-of-place to collect throughout the main campaign!
Puzzles have the same medium difficulty level, which suits really well considering the goal to keep the consistence between releases, not only in the visuals, but as entertaining as possible for previous players.
The Collector's Edition offers a Strategy Guide that may come in hand, and an extra chapter in the story, focused on Gabriel. We finally get to meet him, only to find out how bad he needs our help. This new included DLC journey is well worth it, as it adds a new chapter with some of my favorite scenarios in the game, heavenly inspired by Viking mythology. Everyone loving a good story won't be disappointed, as the interesting and curious backstory to whom Gabriel is will surprise most of you, and possibly make you enjoy the game a lot more.
is a great game but fails to improve on what's really important for future players, the resolution. If one can look over such limitation, it's a great sequel that adds new and interesting content.

I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised by this little gem. It will get compared to Terraria and that's OK because they do live in the same genre but they are vastly different games. I enjoyed Starbound much more because of the story progression. Weapons and armor level up quite nicely with the story, so you never feel underpowered. My only gripe with the story is that the boss fights felt more like an out-heal the dps fest rather than there being skill involved. It is a minor annoyance nonetheless and is ignorable. The crafting is fun as well and materials are a planet's hop away from searching for them. Building wasn't really my forte but I i did build a simple house and had a few inhabitants move in but building that up (along with the ship crew) didn't interest me. If you want to breeze through the story and/or the game itself, you can toggle on the admin mode which makes you invincible and you can make and purchase anything. I would STRONGLY advise against doing this as it takes out the sparkle of the game and should only be done after the story has been completed. There is some end game content and the devs are still adding content so there will always be something to do. For me Terraria had me feeling lost a lot of the time and not sure what to do. Starbound has found a way to let the player be free to do what they want, give them direction on what or where they want to go, and have just the right amount of "randomness".

One of the steepest learning curves I've ever run accross, but holy heck is it worth it! From recreating WW1/2 battleships to then making that battleship FLY, to building a laser spamming death satellite to conquer the world.

An incedible building game. For those who like strategy, engineering, and building games: At 20€ this is a bargain, and on discount a no-brainer.
Now, there are some reservations I woukld hold, however. If you are tight on free time, you won't get much out of it. Designing a single ship can take eight hours or even more. It really eats away your time.
That said, in those eight hours you will get to determine the most fundamental parts of your ship, from the aerodynamic profile of your missiles, the exhaust piping of your engines or the fine adjustments to your warheads.
My tip for you: don't build things blind. Make sure you create a solid modular hardpoint system so that you can just install different engines, cannon systems, or armour layers, rather than having to create a unique design every time. Some pen and paper helps get the design specific things right helps, too.

If you expect this game to be of the same caliber as the sublime
, prepare for bitterest disappointment.  While the fighting is responsive and the PC optimization is excellent, too much of the game is a mess.
The levels, in layout and aesthetic, are by and large atrocious; the magnificent fantasy forests and brooding, vine-choked ruins of the first game have been exchanged for tedious near-future cityscape where 90-degree angles dominate (nice attempt at camouflage with those pretty textures, Mercury Steam, but they can only go so far).   There are a few brief, beautiful segments that take place within Dracula's "inner castle," but these are over too soon and serve to highlight the dull ugliness of the metropolis, which is confusing, repetitive and filled to the boxy margins with generic, endlessly respawning T-Virus monsters.  Yes, you spend most of the game battling urbanites transformed into Biohazard C-stringers by a Satanic biological agent, and they are a dull lot indeed.
The worst gameplay sections of all are the stealth bits.  In these, Dracula, who is supposed to be the baddest damn thing in the world, Dracula, who demolishes building-sized gorgons, Dracula, who ultimately succeeds in deep sixing
, must hide from cyborg guards with plasma rifles who are able to one-shot him on sight!  Aside from making absolutely no sense in terms of the game world, these bitter bits of Metal Gear lite are distinctly unfun.  Hell, you don't even get to kill one of the damn things!  The bad guys should have just sent an army of these cyborg guys after Dracula, thus ensuring the Devil's terrestrial reign forever.
The storytelling in Lords of Shadow 2, like everything else in it, seems patchy and incomplete.  In concept, it was a great idea (you'll see this if you stick it through to the end), but the execution is completely slapdash, leaving even some of the most important plot points, particularly the seemingly transdimensional status of Dracula's castle, unexplained.  Most of the time, you'll be unsure of
you are doing what you are doing.
Despite all, I recommend this -- but only for the price of ten or fewer U.S. dollars, and only if the shockingly fun DLC, Revelations, is included.  Surprised?  Well, as I said, the story isn't bad, it's just badly told for the most part; if you are fan of the first Lords of Shadow, you'll want to the experience the unexpectedly cool ending of LOS2.  Also, most of the boss fights are pretty damned great, particularly the epic final battle!
Lords of Shadow 2 is a poor Lords of Shadow game and kind of a bad Castlevania game, but it's not really a bad
, just a mediocre one with a few redeeming bright spots.  By all means, give it a whirl when it's on sale.

Continuing from the first Lords of Shadow, which had a strong sense of adventure, always moving on, traveling from one end to the other and, apart from the dlc(which I'd advice you to simply ignore entirely), never forces you to backtrack. A feeling of being on an grandious, epic, adventure through ancient lands and fairy creatures as well as monsters. It's was not the most ideal re-imagining of the Castlevania brand, there were the low's but also the high's, and the high's outweighed the low's IMO... that is until they actually continued from the epilogue and explained it.
Lords of Shadow 2 is an oddly excellent example of a game who's budget coupled with one man's over-confidence(from the success of the first game) turned arrogance, effectively ruined any ounce of a future this particular franchise ever had. There is quality here, don't doubt it, it's just found sparsely between thick stretches of game-design that will utterly boggle the mind, how Enric Álvarez, the series director who, literaly, stood for every gameplay design and story sequence in LoS2, how he ever convinced himself this was good.
The combat is more of less the exact same, apart from a few weapons, with an added options to turn off quicktime-events.
The game is split up between modern-times, where you travel through a city which was built around Dracula's grand castle, and past times, before humanity apparently conquered the dark prince, a mystery you will only solve a half-hour before the credits roll. Execution is everything. The story telling, the characters, the level design, the various game mechanics, the leveling system to the weapons... all of it is just horribly miss-matched and all over the place. There are stealth sections equiped with enemies in god-mode. You simply aren't able to fight them and they take you out with projectiles in two hits. These sections are numerous and extremely tedious. You're supposed to be Dracula, taking on Satan himself... but you are apparently a small ant compared to this simple mob. Laughable. PR said that they were going to fuse the first LoS with SotN(one of my favorite games ever) and the thought had me riveting with saliva. I could even see it in front of me.
I loathed the story almost completely. Resented every aspect of the modern levels. Not a fan of this Alucard either apart from purely visual perspective. He even retconned the story from the first game in a pretty stupid way. I bought this at full price day one. I did not listen to reviews. If you think you want this game, re-evaluate, come back after a week or so and if you still want this game... wait for a steamsale, no sense of wasting more money than you have to.

Keeps to the core engagement of the first game, but sands off many of the annoyances. I've only encountered one minor bug and it was patched the next day. The character creator met my expectations, and didn't need to divert more work from the main game.  Your charater's dialouge is more utilitarian than I would like, sometimes to the point of breaking the fourth wall (i.e: "I need another player to hold it open" or "I need to craft a(n) _____ to perform this escape") If I could tweak or change things, I would make the non-perimeter escapes not require you to be holding an item to escape and focus on makeing the interesting or challenging to reach,
Ultimately a very positive experience, and would reccomend it.

Why do I say that? Because this game allows almost anyone to play the game in a style that fits them.
The core gameplay is set up traps, combined with weapons to fight waves of enemies. This games the game two distinct themes, strategy and action. This allows people to play in multiple ways that fit thier favoured playstyles.
Do you want to go full strategy? Use barricades to direct flow into high density traps, with weapons designed for impeding enemy movement in high density areas to maximise the power of your traps.
Want full action? Use one-time-usage traps to compliment an array of weapons to allow you to not need to plan a strategy, and rather deal with issues as they arise.
A mix? Well then you can take as much as you want from as many areas as you want. General purpose weapon, traps throughout the area that compliment your damage as you fight them as they move through.
Thats just a few ideas that immediately came to mind/that I played with.
There is a strong sense of progression, with 'skulls' acting as a persistent currency that you spend into buying different traps and weapons to compliment your playstyle. The skulls are refundable at any point, returning 100% of them so you are free to invest in a different set of traps and weapons or even try a totally different playstyle. This sense of progression manages to fit rpg elements into this already action/strategy hybrid.
Despite mixing so many elements into the gameplay, it plays very fluidly, which is the game's strongest selling point. Strategy and action elements are mixed together without any real noticable seam.
All in all, with a huge variety of gameplay this game can basically cater to anyone. One thing that must be said is that coop makes this game SIGNIFICANTLY better. If you have friends to play with, play with them, its a much improved experience.
All in all, highly reccomended, with a caveat of you should be playing in coop.

If you love vampires (the kind that don't sparkle) then there is really no way to exclude this from your collection, because  when it comes down to it, this is a high budget vampire action game. Whips, swords, claws, and excellent cinematography within the world. Its the first vampire game I've ever played where you truly feel like an immortal being, and time passes in an almost dreamlike way. I personally loved the the parts of the game (about half) spent inside Dracula's Castle, especially walking outside amongst the frozen ramparts with those beautiful gothic spires in the distance, fighting Knights and such. (The whole time not entirely sure whether this castle is an actual place, or it was destroyed and you are simplying battling through your mind palace to reclaim lost memories) If thats the sort of thing that appeals to you, then this game is worth every penny.
The other half of the game is set inside a futuristic post apocalyptic earth; it feels kind of like you're playing a dungeon in "The Secret World" - not badly done, just a strange break of character to fight flying riot police with machine guns after fighting knights in a castle.
The reason I rate this game, especially the original, so low, is because the story and character progression feels like a PS2 game. It is extremely linear; there is very little in the way of character customization or side storylines. The other reason, and this is the main reason, is that the instructions are often very vague and have only one very specific trigger to complete an objective, so you often spend time puzzle solving something relatively mundane. I personally had to look up how to do a lot of things, and it was frustrating. There is also a lot of climbing in the first one for some reason. About 20% of the game feels like a Guild Wars 2 jumping puzzle or an Assassin's Creed exploration mission. Revelations adds a couple of mechanics to shorten this process, but it can still be annoying.
End result is, the more you like vampires, the more you will like this game.

I will be honest, I was skeptical when I first saw this. A 3D desktop in Source that allows the launching of nearly ANY file? Early access or not, I didn't really think such a thing was possible. I could certainly see videos and images being possible, seeing that many Garry's Mod addons have allowed for such a thing before.
I went into this with high expectations, and I must say that this has passed with flying colors.
I can't really call it a "game" since the most you do is interact in a 3D house to open other games and applications. Regardless, this is one of the most intuitive uses of the Source engine I've seen in some time. Being able to creat your own house to use, or even import large maps in, is also a very creative idea, allowing for a lot of variety in house design and layouts. Not to say that the default maps are bad; they certainly do their job rather well. Still, having the option to use other Source maps is appreciated. I haven't tried custom props yet, but if that works, I would certainly call this "Garry's Desktop."
I'm also glad that the game aspect, which was what interested me most, works as it should. You can create a cabinet for any game on your computer, and it's not limited to just Steam. You can add games you downloaded online, emulated roms, or games from other online game stores like Origin (consider it the closest thing to playing Titanfall or PvZ Garden Warfare through Steam we're gonna get so far).
Now for a few negatives of mine. These are just a few issues I had with the program itself, but nothing that people should worry about. To begin, some games have issues running when opened through AA. For example, Team Fortress 2 does play, but it will only let me see the gamemode select. I can't open my server list or favorites. Another 2 small nitpicks is that you can't really use the furniture, and you can't have videos playing when exploring the house. What I mean with the furniture is that you can't sit in it like you could with stuff in Gmod. I understand that it wouldn't have much of a point since people will be on a seperate window or fullscreening a video anyway, but a little attention to detail like that would be nice. As for the videos, you can only play them if you have the screen selected, and I'm not sure why that is the case. It would be nice to be able to have them playing even without the video module selected, especially for a guy like me that likes having music playing in the background while playing PC games.
Outside of that, Anarchy Arcade indeed has lots of potential, and has a lot of things going for it in it's current Early Access form. I hope the developers take this review to heart and continue to improve the game.

The game is overall great when it comes to gameplay, you’re going to be running, jumping, sliding, wall jumping, pen surfing, and fighting enemies as you traverse through "50+ levels" of fun. Controlling "Fancy pants man" has never felt so great, and while I do love how fluid and great the game feels, I just cannot recommend this game in its current state.
(Warning: I’m going to be referring to the console game: "Fancy Pants Adventures" a lot in this review)
Pros
+Controls; very smooth and easy to control
+Combat; although it simple, it’s very satisfying
+Parkour; running, jumping, and sliding all flow together perfectly (Con: why would you take out the direction/height you could wall jump off???)
+Animation and Movement; looks and feels amazing!
+Upgrading you character; adds an extra sense of progression to the game
Cons
-56 levels; some levels actually last 2 seconds while other's usually last 5-10 minutes, honestly they feel more like screens, and it feels very deceptive that the dev(s) called some two second screens "levels". The console version and even the flash versions are perfect examples of what a level should be.
-Enemies; at the first 20 minutes of the game you get so see a large variety of different enemies, but later on all you fight are ink blobs which are not at all difficult to defeat and are frankly boring to fight after a while. You also can’t slide into the ink enemies (making the sliding mechanic feel useless). In the console game, you can battle pirates, ninjas, frogs, crabs, spiders, rats, and more! But here, you’re fighting the same ink enemies throughout the game? (Side note: there are only 4 different types of ink enemies here).
-Level design; compared to "Fancy Pants Adventures", the level design in this game feels very lazy. While in the last game you’re going through a swamp, downtown, a beach, or a cave (and many other places). In this game you’re just running along one color (either purple, orange, red, or green) for a large duration of it. The only place that actually looked different (in a good way) was the tree pirate village.
-Difficulty; The game is way too easy, collecting points refill your health bar way too much and enemies do too little damage when they hit you. It is literally impossible to die in this game, I only died once and that was because I had to purposely jump off a cliff almost 10 times or more just so I can see the death animation. The bad part is that you can also upgrade your health, making the game feel like a chore to beat since there is no danger that can harm you.
-Customization; only 20 pants and hats to collect which is almost nothing compared to the Console version of almost hundreds of items to change on your character including your weapon, pants, and head gear. The amount of customization here is just underwhelming.
-Exploration; One of the things I loved about the console version was how you could take your time and explore the level you’re in to find hidden levels because of how the levels were designed, and while there are hidden levels/challenges here, there isn't much exploring here to do. Unlike the console version, your just running though levels like it was nothing. You’re not really rewarded as much as you were in the last game for exploring, like 100% levels
-The Ending; not going to spoil anything, but the ending left me saying "that was it???".
I really hope the dev(s) are not expecting another $10 for another 2 hours of content...
-Duration of the Game; It defiantly did not last long at all, I spent x10 more time in the console game than in this game. I spent about 5 hours in this game but in reality, this game should take about 2 hours to beat and 3 hours to complete the game fully. There is almost no replayability here unlike the console game, which is the main reason why I really dislike this game.
-Overall content; going to compare it to the console version here again :), the game falls short when it comes to content. The game doesn’t last long to beat, it doesn’t have that many challenges, and it overall just gets boring near the end of the game (which is really bad since it only lasts 2 hours). In "Super Fancy Pants Adventures" you had Bonus levels, Golf, Time Trials, Trick Arenas, King of the Hill tournaments, and HD remastered versions of the flash game (World 1 and 2). Yet here all you receive is a short game and small challenge levels with little difficulty.
Conclusion
This game DEFINATLY does not deserve the name "Super" Fancy Pants Adventure, the only thing this game improved upon was the controls, combat, and animation. Content is very lackluster, little to no difficulty here, no replayability, it was just overall a disappointment from the last game. The developer did state that he will be updating this game and adding new/more challenges and even multiplayer (I was going to put no multiplayer as a con but it will be added later on) and maybe some new game modes, but I doubt it will reach the worth of the regular price it’s asking for. I would not recommend this game for $10 at all.
Now I wouldn't disregard this game altogether, the game is fun, just not $10 worth of fun.
Get this on sale if you like, maybe for $5, but otherwise it’s a no from me.
(Side note: Paid $5 for a "Fancy Key" from the developers site that promised me extra content or something for future fancy pants games like this one on steam:

Yes, in a boldly original move, I've decided to review the sequel right after the original game, if only so I don't have to reintroduce anything.
It's like the first game, only better. Review done?
Seriously though, the sequel managed to address most of my concerns regarding the first game.
The intro tutorial is actually connected to the main plot this time around - Kate (the protagonist) is driving around when the radio tells her the House keeps popping up in the same place and spewing weird fireballs. Thankfully, it's within driving distance - because a spooky mansion that can teleport through space and time will never leave New Jersey (which I guess is an appropriate substitute for eternal damnation). She stops at a gas station and the puzzle has to do with... no, not getting gas for your car. Why would you even think that? That part is handled for you. You have to retrieve the car keys from behind the sun visor (I remind you that we just drove to the gas station), and wash the car's windshield - Kate has suddenly grown very conscious of the dangers of poor visibility. But that's all stuff that doesn't make sense in
, which is a huge improvement over the first game.
The plot is as follows - an enormous evil organ (no, you pervs, the mechanical kind) has taken over the house, and is spewing evil fireballs all the place. The residents assure you that they're deeply concerned. No, really.
The House finally justifies its moniker, by sending you to different times and places that were devastated by the evil fireballs (that don't really do anything of the sort in the house itself, because various rooms have backgrounds that are set in stone). You need to complete such fiendish puzzles as "brew some rose tea for the ghost" and "find all the animal figurines" in order to retrieve the [s]crystal[/s] skull hidden in each such location. The locations are fairly arbitrary, but it's nice to get out of the house and hang out in Tibet / Indiana Jones style lost temples / Roman-era Jerusalem.
Other improvements - the hints come back much faster this time around (half the time it took in the original). Once you've retrieved the skull in certain era, it's closed off for exploration, so you don't get lost, wondering whether the fan is meant to blow out the flames over the bird nest in Paris, or to shoo away the moths from the portrait in the pirate fortress. The map is right next to the hint button, instead of being hidden away in the journal section - much handier (my mom didn't even find the map during her first playthrough of the original), particularly since the game tends to double-dip into hidden object screens - you'll complete one in order to find a specific object, and a few puzzles later you'll have to do it all over again, finding a different set of items this time around.
So this is a fairly major improvement over the original.

This game is effectively "dead" except for the admittedly fun single player/local multiplayer.
That said onto the review:
I used to own this on the ps3 when it came out and...
I forgot how much the AI ♥♥♥♥ing cheats in this game.
There is no rear vision mirror, this is because the game developer doesnt want you to see the cars teleporting in behind you.
There is no Speedometer, this is because the game developer doesnt want you to know the speed stats are a lie.
The car stats you see and what the AI has are two completely different things.
If you plan to win the only important stats are accelleration & toughness, having a higher top speed just means the AI's topspeed on all cars is better than yours, drafting stat isnt really that important provided its above 3~ so you can turn your car goodly.
Infact the BETTER cars in the game are the ones with high acelleration and comparatively LOW top speed, you unlock one early with 1 speed and 5 accel, this car has the best chance of winning at all levels (in race or elimination vs AI not humans) with heavy use of ingame traps as the AI slows itself down so you dont fall too far behind.
Your high accelleration means you can stay on the AI and draft to build power alot more easily, and your low speed means you'll actually see the racer in first place instead of him been 8+ seconds ahead the entire race even though you you never crashed your car or ♥♥♥♥ed up.
Simply, if you dont want to play against SUVs that are invulnerable to explosions and outpace your lamborghini-esque car, do not use a lamborghini-esque car, use a shitbox with good accelleration.
The AI also will not EVER attempt to use explosions/traps on other AI they only target you making getting into 2nd-1st extermely difficult as they've had a free run for the first half/entire lap because no matter what car you use (even on revisited early races with endgame cars) the AI is ALWAYS faster than you off the mark by 2-3seconds and then goes uncontested/unblocked for a decent amount of time.
The power play mechanic is badly implemented and makes been in first place actually detrimental to your chances of winning the race as the only ways to consistantly gain speed is to
1. Turn poorly and draft which allows the speedhacking AI to easily overtake you as you're turning wide/slowing down.
2. Not be in first place and follow someone for 10+ seconds
3. Almost get him by AI traps (only way to gain power while in first place)
To actually win in this game you need to tail the AI in first place and kill him right at the end using traps or expect to randomly get overtaken right before you win by an SUV that according to ingame stats is worse in every single stat comparatively to your god car.
Oh, and the AI will NEVER attempt to blow each other up at all, ever. Its basically a 1v7 race where the goal of 6 of the cars is to delay you so the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in firstplace can get an impossible lead or remove all your power so you cant kill said ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
In summary its a very fun CASUAL "blow all the cars up simulator" i honestly cannot call this a racing game, because for it to be a racing game you would place depending on player skill, and in the single player campaign that is not how the game works.
The detonation/survival/airstrike etc gamemodes are probably the most fun/repeatable features you can play in singleplayer/competitively with a friend because there isnt any AI to cheat and its argueably "skill" based. That is until you run into impossible airstrike patterns because the helicopter decided that the small 2lane section of racetrack right after a corner where you are is a perfect spot to drop 8+ missiles.

The pros:

-Good music
-Good concept/story

Seems like most of the things I have criticized in my old review are fixed now. There were updates every week, with tons of bug fixes, optimizations and even new content. They switched now to a 2 week update cycle with even more stuff. The game is still far from beeing perfect, keep that in mind. But I can't deny that the dev's are working hard on the updates and the game is getting better and better. So, I cann actually recommend the game now, if you're into FPS games and a fan of weapon customization. But keep in mind that HO is still in Early Access, so there are still bugs and stuff to fix.
OLD REVIEW:
The first time I heard of Hired Ops was in the Escape from Tarkov forum. Someone mentioned it and said it's from the same Dev's, so I went to Facebook and played a few rounds. The old version of Hired Ops was called "Contract Wars" and was a F2P game on plattforms like Facebook vKontakte etc. I can't say if it was a so called "Pay To Win" game or not, because I played only 3-5 matches in total. (I had to reinstall Firefox, because my Chrome couldn't use the Unity Player for some reason). I was pretty impressed by the overall quality of the game. The animations, the visuals and especially the gun sounds were pretty good. Especially for a F2P game. The gameplay felt a bit clunky to me, because I play most of my FPS with "Hold ADS", but the overall gameplay was decent.
So, here we go with Hired Ops. The standalone version of Contract Wars, devoloped by AbsoluteSoft instead of Battlestate Games like it's predecessor.
To keep things as short as possible, here is a Pro/Con list:
- Graphics. The game looks absolutely gorgeous. There are still some visual bugs, like the Anti Aliasing not affecting everything on the map, but the overall graphics quality is very good.
- High quality sounds and animations.
- Recoil. Re What? Yes. The guns in the game actually have recoil. And it feels pretty nice imo.
- Leaning mechanics. Well, even COD4 had it back in the days but in HO, it's actually very useful
- Good amount of guns
- Very detailed weapon customization
- Night maps that are actually dark. Dark AF to be honest. There are things like NVG's and weapon flashlights though. They don't need to be unlocked and can be used by everyone.
- Pretty good perfomance for most of the time. I'm playing with 60-90 FPS with pretty much everything maxed out. (FX 8350, R9 290, 8GB Ram, Windows 10 64 Bit) BUT(!)
I had one match, where the whole game started to lag. (In terms of FPS and Network connection), resulting in a complete crash of my PC. I've read something about a possible memory leak, so maybe that was the problem.
- Weapon unlocks. I know it's a controversal topic in FPS games and some people like them because they like the motivation and challenge  and some (like me) don't like them because it's kinda unfair to give people who have a higher rank an advantage, because they can buy better guns and attachments. It's up to you. It didn't felt like the other people had way better guns though, but I still prefer to have all guns right from the beginning.
- No HP Regeneration. Personally, I prefer to have no HP reg, because it makes gunfights more intense and realistic. But some people may not like it, so I put it in the neutral area.
- "Killstreaks" Don't be scared. It's not as bad as it sounds. There are only two of them. The 3 kills streak, which gives you a sonar (Kinda like a UAV, but you have to put it on the map by yourself like a granate and it's range is pretty small), and a mortar strike, which didn't seem to be overpowered to me. At least on bigger maps.
- Skilltree You can unlock things like a faster reload or a bit less recoil. I managed to kill people with higher levels but since it could be considered as an unfair advantage, I listed it as neutral.
- Bugs:
The game is in Early Access, so I expect the game to have some bugs. But I don't want to ignore them either. I already mentioned the missing Anti Aliasing on some objects, but there are some other things like the wierd collision detection on some objects. As example: On Bay, if you try to jump on the container, your feet just slip away from the edge instead of landing on it.
The hit detection pretty awkward on some servers. It just feels laggy sometimes and the fact that some servers are pretty laggy doesn't help either. I had one match with a 150+ ping, even though the server should be located in Frankfurt and my ping should be fine.
I had one match, where I co♥♥♥♥♥ed my controls midgame and couldn't use my mouse after leaving the menu. There is also some small visual bug, where your mouse cursor get's duplicated multiple times in front of a black screen / loading screen. It's not a serious problem, but it's a bug none the less.
- Frustrating spawns, especially on small maps like Bay. Spawning right in front of enemys is not cool.
- The matchmaking puts me on servers with a 150+ Ping sometimes.
-
(Patched)
So, yeah. I think the game has some potential, because it's a good mix of components from fast-paced arcade FPS like CoD or Battlefield and more realistic FPS games like Arma, Insurgency etc. The game needs some serious polishing and bug fixing, but if all my mentioned points are fixed in the future, I think it will be a pretty decent FPS game.
it's up to the Dev's now to stay active and release patches, bug fixes and more content, until the game is in a good state for the release.
So, can I recommend the game? I wasn't sure the first time, but after playing the game a few more times, I tend to say no. At least not now. I like the concept, the visuals, the customization etc. and tbh, I had some pretty cool and intense gunfights, but some bugs are just too frustrating and people shouldn't rely on the hope that everything that's wrong right now will be fixed in the future. I won't refund the game right now and wait for the next weeks for more patches and bugfixes. If most of the stuff I mentioned is fixed, I will change my recommendation to "yes", because all these bugs aside, I think it's a pretty good game.

Debilitatingly disappointing. I can't stand this crap pile of code. The story is excruciatingly slow. The dialogue is awkward and is comprised mostly of overly-exaggerated acting.
The graphics are sub-par. Even on the highest settings on a newer high-end Samsung plasma TV and a gaming PC equipped with SLI'd GTX 780 Ti's, I am reminded more of a PS3 game than a PC game. After much experimentation with the graphic settings, I have come to the conclusion that they used motion blur to cover up the shortcomings and inadequacies of their game engine. Motion blur has clearly been implemented to bridge and smooth the gaps between stuttering frames rather than to create a more realistic sense of motion. (Turn off motion blur and you'll see what I mean.)
The combat gameplay is utterly terrible. Gabriel is incredibly sluggish for being the badass that he's supposed to be. The camera angles are unmanageable and frequently interfere with the direction of your attack. Even the minor improvement after you disable the "Combat Assist Camera" setting, you are still left to struggle against some unidentified form of 'aim-assist' that frequently targets random objects to your sides and behind you rather than the bad guys - which is completely infuriating.
On that note, let's talk about enemies. Enemies are as cheap as they come. Their attacks will always interrupt yours where, conversely, your attacks rarely ever interrupt theirs. To make matters worse, the enemies constantly rely mostly on their 'unblockable' attacks. They are so frequent that fighting multiple groups of monsters results in more dodging and - invariably - dying over and over again rather than a well-balanced challenge. The unblockables are either back-to-back or followed up by a second attack that changes oblique angles to follow Gabriel in more of a 'homing' fashion. All of this requires a lot more room to maneuver than is often provided.
Forget blocking. It worked well in the first game but here, blocking is inconsistent in success.
Worse still; as you progress through the game, you are faced with armored enemies whom you can not damage until you fist-pound the armor off of their bodies with the chaos claws. (This supposedly makes the armor "hot" until it either shatters...OR the AI decides that it's too hot to wear - at which point they strip it off.)
Attacks don't just glance off of the armor. They bounce off. This makes targeting the lesser enemies around an armored enemy IMPOSSIBLE as your blows land squarely on the armored enemy rather than on any of the non-armored enemies. This makes fighting infuriating as you can't target the armored enemy without having to constantly avoid the attacks of the lesser enemies and vise versa. (Again, most of these attacks are unblockables.)
It is also obvious that the developers generate challenge in the game using cheap methodology. The whip's reach is ridiculously short and enemies purposefully stay just outside of it's range. The sword and claws are nearly useless as they are limited on usability due to rapidly-drained energy meters which must be saved for various tasks. It's also irritating that ground attacks still catch you in-air - despite what basic relativity/logic would otherwise dictate.
The bosses are ridiculous with typical lather/rinse/repeat tactics. Many of their attacks feel cheap and, at first, unavoidable. (Again, Gabriel is ridiculously sluggish.)
Also... Why is a terrible creature such as Dracula spending so much time skulking in the dark as a rat? LAME.
Then there are the little maze/stealth 'puzzle games' you play with various main story characters. (Carmella, Agreas (Pan's brother,) etc.) Here, you have to sneak through the areas unseen as the characters hunt you with intent to kill you on sight. These are incredibly irritating. This is NOT what Castlevania games are about. The controls are difficult enough but these control difficulties are highlighted during these maze/stealth puzzle games.
All of this does little more than to make your character seem weak and not AT ALL like someone who once defeated the most powerful foes the world's history has ever known. This is unforgivable.
It definitely wasn't long into the game to realize that it's an atrocity. Not only does it quickly prove you right, it actually makes you realize that you underestimated it's terrific level of crappiness. It's definitely the type of game that makes you wonder in fury if the studio has ever heard of "quality assurance." ("Did they even PLAY the damn game after making it!?")
NOTE: Dying finds you having to re-watch all videos and re-gather all items you find unless you passed a save point - including shards that increase your stats. (WHY, Mercury Steam? WHY!?)
Don't feel bad if you finally give up on playing this crappy game and resort to Googling the videos to finish Gabriel's story instead. Trust me. I should have. It's NOT worth the time it takes to play it.

I really wanted to like this game.  I enjoyed Adventure Capitalist and have beaten it twice on my phone already (and working on beating the Steam version for PC.)  Adventure Communist though, just leaves me wondering why I'm playing it, and thinking "this is not fun".
Now it's free, so I'm not expecting a lot, but I don't want to play a game that's not a least a little fun.  I can deal with a lot of grinding, that was pretty much the core mechanic  of Adventure Capitalist.  The straw that broke the camel's back for me with AdComm was the way research is handled.  Research is the key that unlocks great advances, you get 20-25 research points a day grinding through the 15 daily challenges (which involve clicking a few thousand times).
So you can unlock a means of getting free research points, and I discovered two things:  That it was going to give me one research point every 4 hours, which felt like a cheap shot since all the previous things cycle in seconds or less than 10 minutes, but ok.  Second, you get 1 research point and then you have to LOG IN to start the cycle again.  Which is crap IMHO.  Most of us have better things to do than babysit an idle clicker game to log in every 4 hours.  Well, at least I do.
In summary, not fun, and once you  reach the end game which takes so much grinding to get to, they change the rules.  No thanks, I'm done with this dud.

Starships starts out relatively fun - you can work your way up through the difficulty chain and the map size while trying out different factions and characters. However, after about 2 hours of play the game becomes extremely repetitive. I have played multiple missions at the highest difficulty with the largest map size and always win - gameplay just becomes a grind, really. I find that torpedoes are the weapon of choice, especially when combined with the wonder that allows 2 actions per turn and the wonder that cloaks torps.
Graphics are simple but clean. Sound is good for what it is. The in-game movies for certain events (like firing torps) gets old because it wastes time. The game is very stable - has not crashed at all.
The real problem with the game is as I stated in the first paragraph - it is an easy game. It is also simple (not complex), which is a good thing, but the ease of the game means that there is no real replay value. All your games will pretty much be the same, and therefore become more of a grind than a fun experience.
Rating 7/10 (8/10 initially, 4/10 later on)

It is repetative, essentially relying on a singular game mechanic where you pilot a single type of ship through about 5 puzzles. There is a maze, a capture and control, a hunt, etc. The ship types are naught, you get a ship that has a largely linear upgrade path. While I could have plenty of fun on the bus with my tablet, on my PC this game feels like solitaire plus. A let down. Now, while this doesn't cost as much as a landmark game it still could have more flavor. The civilizations feels like different theme colors, and the technologies and cash have a more passive feel than I'd like.

Personally I had a lot of fun playing through this game, as I loved the original games and especially enjoyed playing the Xbox game with my friends back when that came out. The controls feel amazing and fluid (I played with a controller) and the combat system was simple yet fun, and was a nice step up from the combat system on the Xbox game. The new additions to this game are great, and I love the level designs, simple as they may be. The music is pretty good too, although a bit repetitive at times. As well as the great gameplay, the game is also very quick to load up and puts you right back in the area you were last in, so you are ready to go immediately without having to navigate a menu first.
One thing to keep in mind, however, is that I have finished the story, collected every item and earned every achievement in just 3 and a half hours of play time. As much fun as I had playing it, I now feel like there is no replayability to it, other than to grind for more squiggles to buy the rest of the health and power upgrades, which isn't really worth it if there isn't anything else to play through. I don't really mind this as the experience of playing through the game was great for me, but keep in mind how short the game is when deciding whether or not to buy the game.

This game is a lot of fun. it's a fast paced platformer that rewards quick reaction and cleaver use of momentum. the developer has been developing and polishing the engine for many years and it really shows. the movement is smooth as butter and flows really nicely, also complimented by good level design. while the art style is simplistic the animations are extremely nice. However the game is pretty short and feels unfinished because of a few things..
it ends with a "too be continued", there's many things about the story and world that remain unresolved and unexplained and there's an area called the bathtub tower which seems to have been intended to be a central home area of sorts. it has 5 floors. early in the game you'll unlock a shop on the 1st floor that you can buy upgrades from. there's nothing to do on the other floors yet but certain things lead you to expect there will be, for example on the second floor there's an empty bar area and on the 3rd a bunch of blank arcade machines. the camera zooms into these areas like there's something to interact with but by the end of the game nothing changes. only level 1 of the tower serves a purpose. like i said the game is still fun, in fact I found my self replaying levels and challenge doors multiple times. it's fun just to roam around and play with the mechanics. I only wish the game had a main menu or a better hub area where i could replay all the challenges in one place.
Also  an odd little thing i found. the game runs in flash but for some reason the .exe blocks access to helpful features like resizing and quality scaling.

Outrun and its sequels are arcade classics. This is a series that's all about driving all over the world in an expensive sports car. It's just you, the road, and the love of your life. Even when you're not behind the wheel of a Ferrari, your car has the top down, so both the driver and the passenger are visible. This is a minor detail, but it really adds to the sense of escapism. In Outrun 2, the girlfriend is very expressive, cheering on your successful driving skills, and getting annoyed when you bump into cars. While it's easy to say that the Outrun games are great, due to their fantastic controls and solid game-design, it's the tone and atmosphere that really bring it all together.
Outdrive is...well I'm going to be serious here. Outdrive is a twisted metaphor for keeping a loved-one on life-support. In the intro, your girlfriend is shot during a hired hit, a drug deal gone bad, or actually... nevermind. The reason is irrelevant. Basically, she's going to die, and there's nothing you can do about it. Even knowing this, you hook her up to your car's engine to keep her alive. This isn't a temporary measure; you aren't going to get her to the hospital or anything. The purpose of this game is to drive for as long as possible, until you either go too slow, too fast, or realize the futility of it all and pull the plug.
I hate to go on a moral tangent in a videogame review, but I'm just calling it like I see it. After hooking your girlfriend up to your car, the only signs of life she exhibits are open eyes and in-between songs you can hear some breathing. Granted, she was mortally wounded only minutes ago, but she's already in what could be considered a vegetative state. It would be different if she spoke, or showed some awareness. Maybe she would talk about what happened, use her last moments to reflect upon better times, etc. It's not like her condition will improve, so why do this? So the two of you can sit in silence and listen to synth-music while looking at the neon li-everything?
Oh right, the game portion, I nearly forgot to talk about this. In short, the controls are awful. As the other reviews have stated, keyboard-only is the way to go, because you have to constantly boost to keep the girl alive. For whatever reason, the gamepad doesn't function properly. Steering is problematic, and drifting sends you into just as many walls as not-drifting. Oddly enough, your speed doesn't actually matter. As long as you have your finger on the boost, and are making at least some forward (and sometimes even backward!) progress, then the girl will stay "alive". It's entirely possible to drive at 10-15 mph and it wouldn't affect anything. After about eight and a half minutes, a helicopter appears to shoot at you. This can cause debris to block your path, but it's mostly ineffective. Although, I will point out that the first time the girl died was because I got stuck in debris, the car flipped upside-down, and everything started spazzing out.
By the way, when your girlfriend dies, the game says that you killed her. What? Maybe it's the driver finally accepting the inevitable, and realizing he was wrong to put someone he cares about in such a dangerous situation in the first place. You can also hit the "r" key at any time. This is considered the kill button. Now I'm not even sure what the game's intentions are supposed to be. Pressing the "r" key causes the game to instantly restart, and you don't recieve a "You killed her" message for that. This is what I get for reading too far into things, because now the game is just throwing me for a loop. By the way, if you're driving too fast or slow, your girlfriend will suffer from intense pain. Yes, the game posts a message saying as much whenever you restart.
Outdrive isn't just a bad driving game, it's also really depressing. What's the point of playing this game for a long period of time? To brag to others that you kept a dying person alive - possibly against their will - for an hour or two? This is nothing more than a hollow and extremely selfish accomplishment. Just let her go. It's difficult to accept, but it's better this way. I don't mean to delve into these serious subjects, but within minutes of playing, the realization hit me, and I started to feel absolutely horrible. Nobody deserves to be treated like this.
So.... yeah... Anyone up for a game of CrotchFighter?

GNARLY GAME -- and not in a good way.
You can only play OutDrive using keyboard controls, which are overly sensitive, so your car turns 90 degrees into a wall if you're not very, very careful. Maintaining control of the car is difficult given how keys have been mapped -- very cramped. You can re-map the controls, but this kind of game really needs controller support. In this day and age, for this type of game, not including PROPER controller support is just lazy.
And for those of you that say that you CAN use a controller ... well, it is not working properly for me. For example, when using the boost, which you absolutely need for this game, I can see it's working, but the game doesn't seem to recognize it, so I die anyway.
To survive, you must keep your speed within a certain band -- you can't drive too slow or too fast for extended periods or game over. I can understand a mechanism that encourages the player not to go too slow, but too fast is a problem ...? Totally lame mechanism.
I was hoping for an OutRun-like game ... simplistic but enjoyable driving, but OutDrive is not fun at all. Don't be swayed by the cool graphics, which are definitely amazing. But the game itself is boring and frustrating, with terrible controls. Classic case of a game that have some interesting ideas and looks gorgeous, but fails in execution and gameplay. OutDrive does not deserve your money when so many better games are out there.

I personally have really enjoyed this game, but there are a few things I'd like to point out:
(There are positives, don't panic, they'll come later)
UPDATE: The memory leak issue has apparently been fixed, and the option to choose a matchmaking region and to expand search parameters is now available. Thanks devs!
1) This is not a major issue, but sometimes when starting a new mach, the starting music would play itself 3 times over, with a 0.5 second delay for each 'layer' of the song, and the mouse would leave a cursor trail. This also happens in game, where I would respawn but still be looking out of my dead body (I know I'm alive because I can fire and see my character moving around on the minimap). Additionally, some of the key inputs seem to toggle on or off at random sometimes. For example, upon respawn I once found myself unable to move, ADS (Aim down sights) and jump. All I could do was look around and fire. I had to commit suicide with my grenades, and this impacted my K/D severely. It happened multiple times during the match and become extremely frustrating. Also, I found that sometimes I had to press RMB 2-5 times to ADS, which became hard to work with in intense CQB situations.
2) In terms of gameplay, I understand that the devs have gone for realism. In that case, please add some kind of basic parkour mechanic, such as vaulting over obstacles or climbing a suface, even if it is a selected surface (such as a ladder). I want this because, unfortunately like Contract Wars, the jumping feature sucks. Realistically, no one winds up their legs like a spring for that long and then propels themself into the air swaying their torso like they're drunk. As a CS:GO player, this is hard for me to say.... but, I regret to inform you that COD did this at a half-decent level. You have the option to vault over a small barricade or to quickly hop up onto a step-like surface of some kind. If this was implemented that would be great, and would make the game a lot more realistic and smooth. And if you're going fro weird jack-in-the-box jumping, then at least don't make the camera cut to around everywhere, it's very disorientating and gives some people headaches.
3) Please, don't pair me with all the level 20+ people. They're weapons are so much better than my bare M4A1 and 90two (all of which I had at the time) and it's really hard to get kills when you are mauled by a fully customised ARC-C. Contract Wars had perfectly fine level restricted matches. Even just 0-10 matches would make me happy.
4) Here's a new one, no one plays the game. Seriously, most times I join Steam Charts says that there's >10 people online at that given moment. That's ridiculous! Most people have bought the game and turned it in instantly because it was 'too hard' or 'too laggy' not realising that it's Early Access and things can be worked on, or they mega rage quit and just couldn't get good so they returned the game. And then they write a negative review. All the short fused people are ruining the rep of this game.
Now, onto the positives:
1) The game is amazingly realistic compared to other shooters, which I really love. The gameplay differs from most online FPS games making it something you have to commit to learning how to properly play it to get the best experience. The players in game act a lot more cautiously and think about their decsions more, making the game a lot more enjoyable.
2) I love the new weapon customisation, because it's much easier to operate and achieve as compared to Contract Wars (which I've played for a while), and I also love the fact that they removed weapon repairing. I know I said I love a game to be realistic, but in this circumstance it's just a pain and I'm glad that the devs heard the community about that
3) The changes to gameplay are amazing. You now have free access to NVG, which really helps in those night matches. However, the best new feature is probably sprinting, and I don't think I need to tell you why that's a good thing. Leaning is also great, as people play the game properly now rather than running around like morons spraying their SMGs everywhere while the people who try to take caution are getting murdered. Now you actually have to take cover and be aware of your surroundings
4) THE NEW RECOIL IS AWESOME!!! I know it's harder to control now, but that means you can't just have some idiot buy a Kedr and wreck all the assault rifle and shotgun users. You actually have to manually correct the recoil of your sprays with your mouse, meaning some little kid can't just pick up the game and be a nuisance, you actually have to take the time to learn how to play.
5) The graphics and sounds are absolutely stunning. Honestly, the level of detail and clarity in the audio and graphics are absolutely breathtaking and it's one of the reasons why this game is so appealing to me
6) UPDATE: At long last, you can pick your matchmaking region! This allows much faster games and allows you to actually play without getting teleported everywhere. There is now also the party function, so you can team up with friends and play matches together which is awesome
I'm not going to complain about the lack of variety because the game is still focusing on testing its core components before reaching that level, but in future I would like to see larger maps so the snipers could have a better time, more guns, gun tiers and more customisation options as it would bring a stronger tactical element to the game which I would rather enjoy.
All the gameplay changes have made the game a much better experience. Although there are a few kinks to be worked out, it is still Early Access so people shouldn't get too angry at all the problems; they will be solved eventually. I'm willing to stick by the game and see it grow, as it seems really awesome and I'd be interested to see how far it will get.

Honestly, i was going through a lot of these reviews, expecially from fans of the first game, and i was surprised by how much negatives came here. So this review will be focused in comparing the two games (I played the first on X360)
I will say that, only in my first 2 hours of gameplay, i felt comfortable to rely on the lore for my so expected ending of the story. And i need to point out that this is a great game, regardless of comparations with the first. Also, a lot of these reviews say negative stuff about the stealth moments,
I feel like these moments show me that like in the first game, i had to become strong. Playing all the game with ultimate Dracula powers would be tiring, and most likely ruin the experience.
As to graphics, my system is not the best, but what i've seen in my game and videos, it doesn't leave a lot to be wished.
I really enjoyed the new mechanics of gameplay, especially Gabriel's (sorry, can't call him Dracula :////) new powers. this really feels like to play the first game, but much more complete than that. Something i dislike strongly is the new combat rythim, i can't get to use special attacks, because i'm 95% busy finding enough time to do so. Also, there are some times when you truly don't know what to do, and you have to perform some action too quickly. I found this very troublesome in some parts.
And the camera, oh, the camera. That's something MUCH better than in the first game, when the camera was placed in map-specific locations, and also had the problem of having to stop to ajust your controls, since they were kept on camera changes (40% of camera changes). Now, it's something much more subtle, the camera is controlled by the player, and stays in a 2nd/3rd person view which receives some influence in a few map areas (but nothing that forces the camera on a spot or a too strong change. It feels better because now it gives me the immersion of exploring the world. And of course, this is better because now i feel rewarded for looking for a nice view and finding an amazing view. It's very balanced.
I do recommend this game to everyone, best buy, worth all the money (altough i got it on a discount).

So like, I played this game a lot, I have fond memories of coping depression with it, and it influenced me a lot in my artistic pursuits.
It's not a perfect game but I guess I can write a few pros and cons from memory. They wont alter my final result of saying the game was overall a positive recommendable experience:
PROS:
-Its a rewarding experience if you stick with it, despite the challenging appearence and the marketing heavily implying its crushing difficulty, the game is designed to reward above all else patience and persistance.
-It "would" allow for the crafting of your own theories on how the story is thanks to the (at the time relatively unused) way which it delivers story bits, the so called "Lore" that exists seasoned throught various item descriptions and enviormental storytelling in the game.
(I say "would" because after extensive theory by the fans over the years its hard to come up with something someone hasnt come up with and the sharing of more fantastical or out there theories tends to be looked upon not so great by the community)
-The visuals and imagery are enjoyable, its not the most powerful graphics testing device but it has visually stunning moments.
Cons:
-To someone never having experienced the heaps of fan created media, this game would require actively going against how they teach you to play it to find it a more rewarding and less slow experience.
-It also may actively encourage you to exploit what are essentially flaws in the game design to your advantage, while this can be seen as a con, I am the kind of person that enjoying breaking games like that.
-While the idea of everything being hard but fair sounds cool in theory, in practice games will always have bugs, theres is always the possibility of something happening that is just kind of a♥♥♥♥♥♥move but its not even the developers fault, its just something no one could have predicted.
Extra info:
--It's story is suprisingly enough, if you peel the "lore" and enviormental story telling out of it, pretty meh:
[SPOILER WARNING]
1-Everything is gray dull and filled with dragons and zombies(?).
2-Flames pops up from nowhere and grants powers for reasons unknown.
3-Giants(?) from nowhere grab shards of the fire and gain magic powers.
4-A Dragon mad at the other Dragons helps the Giants(?) kill off the Dragons race.
5-The Giants(?) then have a golden age with some color to it (like literally things stop being grey).
6-Twist! turns out some of the zombies(?) grabbed the titular "Dark soul" from the fire too.
7-The Giants(?) and Zombies(?) arent friends cause the big boys want to be all powerful.
8-Giants(?) curse Zombies(?) into immortality so they can suffer, this hubris eventually comes back to them.
9-the Flames powers now fading (for reasons unexplained) the Giants(?) try everything to keep it running, they kinda fail and cause the closest thing to an apocalypse possible by mistake.
10-the Zombies(?) now go around killing the weak Giants(?) to end their good times and possibly start good times for themselves or just cause it go back to boring ol' grey.
Note: I say "Giants(?)" because later on there turns out there are even larger giants so like I dunno, and I also say "Zombies(?)" because while technically they are more like revenants they also were never really alive or dead to begin with they kinda just... were...
[SPOILER WARNING/]
-Begining nothing is happening, then magic happens and some people profit from it, then the weaker people get a chance to strike back and do so... theres no real like moral dilemma, even though the game gives you the choice to just end everything and make everything go back to being boring and mindless, there is no real reason to do that, as the player character you are one of the Zombies(?), so like why would you not strive to better the world you live in?
-Now it is a bit nitpicky of me to say its a not so great story, but everything really cool or interesting that you could experience has kind of already happened, and that does make sense with the theme sure, but as a game it leaves you to read into cooler stuff that could be happening but that you cant really play through...
--This is not really a game you can play in short bursts so you kind of would have to make time to play it, and that to someone that has little time free is not the easiest.
--Finally, something to note, this game has 2 sequels, named accordingly, and while they are in base simillar games, they can become very different experiences, I played DS1 first and wasnt that into it, then played DS2 and enjoyed it enough to try and replay the first one, then ending up enjoying the first one too, later I got to try DS3 but never really finished it completely but I still enjoyed it. the 3 have gameplay diferences that change quite a bit and suprisingly enough the second game ends up kind of having the biggest impact in the story with its DLC... but anyways.
Overall I cant give this game like too hard a critisim in my mind because I do love this game, it was a pretty important part of my life and like I said helped me cope with something I still fight with to this day, it was overall a fun time.
PS:I am bound to have written a huge ammount of typos, it happens but I hope that even if this was a bit all over the place it was a fun read for those that read it, have a good day/night.
